having an equal share. Said of things equal in size or weight:

as Turnebus wrote. But what is read in M, ἰσοτιμοιρον [equal in honor] (without accent), is more probably conflated from ἀντίμοιρον [having a share instead] and its gloss ἰσόμοιρον [having an equal share], which Erfurdt understood in his note on Soph. El. v.86 (where ὦ φάος ἁγνὸν καὶ γῆς ἰσόμοιρ᾽ ἀήρ [O holy light and air equal in share with earth]). Other examples of the adjective ἀντίμοιρος [having a share instead] are not found except the proper name Ἀντίμοιρος [Antimoerus] and the words ἀντιμοιρεῖν [to have a share instead] (which Pollux 4, 176 explains by ἰσομοιρεῖν [to have an equal share] and L. Dindorf restored to Demosthenes p. 946, 28 in the Thesaurus vol. 1, 2 p. 942) and ἀντιμοιρία [a share in return].
